threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think googling 'best coffee' will help you find the right spot. It's all about who you know and the whispers in the queue.
Caught a guy on the 333 last night narrating his life story to a bemused cat in a carrier. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a kid selling lemonade at Karl-Marx-Straße, while a couple was having a heated debate about the best Döner in town.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you see people doing yoga on the tram during rush hour, completely unfazed by the chaos around them.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local if they know the best times to avoid Dolores Park when the food trucks show up. Outsiders? They just flock on weekends, clueless about the lines.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full suit eating a burrito on the bus while an accordion player serenaded the last stop. Only in the TL, folks.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the street performers are just fun, but some are actually locals making a living. It's a fine line between art and survival here.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how they still look confused trying to figure out the taquilla at the metro. Regulars glide right by.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still don’t know the secret cafe behind the barbershop on Kingsland Road. Trust me, the espresso’s a game-changer.
Last night on the 59, a lad proposed to his girlfriend at Stockwell. The whole bus cheered, but she just sat there, completely blank-faced.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw an old man feeding pigeons with a slice of pizza in the middle of a protest—no one batted an eye. That's when I knew I belonged.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a techno party inside a former public toilet—complete with graffiti and a proper bar. The spirit of Berlin is truly underground.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they casually step over the dog that's taken a nap on the Muni tracks like it's just a part of their morning commute.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 14 after the BART chaos. A guy started rapping about the delays, everyone chuckled. Only in SF do we turn transit misery into a live show.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the trendy bars, but locals know it's the neighborhood's unassuming bakeries that keep the heart beating.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones wandering around with a map in hand, still trying to figure out how to navigate the winding streets of Gràcia without GPS.
